question: Does enumerating all concentration contexts improve curve MAE at the same scalar-row and boosting-iteration training budget?
status: frozen before new ablation training or scoring
dataset: EPA NFA, 243 chemicals, 4 DIV x 17 endpoints

evaluation.test_designs: unchanged five published seeded contexts from designs(task,3)
evaluation.metric: curve MAE averaged within chemical over published contexts; each chemical one bootstrap observation
evaluation.delta: full enumeration minus five-design row-matched; negative favours enumeration

arms.full: Reuse byte-frozen published full-enumeration per-chemical errors; source SHA, recipe and train rows verified per fold. Retain historical elapsed time as historical, not same-machine time.
arms.five_matched: For each training chemical, build only the five original published design rows in original order. Let F be its number of valid scalar target rows over all contexts, and R its corresponding five-design count. Repeat each of these R rows floor(F/R) times, then add one copy of F mod R rows chosen by a seeded permutation; physically materialize F rows. Seed=first 8 hex digits of SHA256(chemical|rowmatch|3). This matches each chemical and fold scalar-row budget exactly.
arms.five_unmatched_reference: Previously published five-design-only 600-iteration run retained separately; excluded from the primary budget-matched claim.

resource.probe: first 12 non-fold-1 chemicals in source order; 20 iterations, no test scoring
resource.termination: each finite fold fit and its fixed test list completes, or 300s local hard stop; failed attempts retained

budget_interpretation: Equal materialized scalar training rows, feature width and 600 boosting iterations. Unique rows and design coverage differ by construction. Histogram binning, tree structure and wall-clock time may differ. No test tuning or selection.
